verdict.note: 46/46 on node:sqlite 3.51.3, including the multi-process vectors: 8 processes cold-opening one fresh database migrate it exactly once, 4 consumers split 300 messages with no double dequeue, and a cursor advanced during 6 concurrent writers saw all 720 messages exactly once. 3556 enqueues in 10.00s, p50 2.927ms p99 6.136ms.

7/7 flips gated; every reported failure is one of the contract's own assertions naming the violated claim, not environment noise. Guard verified against reality in the same run: an engine that cannot load produces only the file-level summary line, which is exactly the predicate stubs/run.mjs classifies as HARNESS FAILURE and exits non-zero on, so an unmeasured decision cannot appear as a measured one.

40/40 through better-sqlite3 13.0.3 with only the binding swapped; the migration SQL hashes identically under both drivers (4466bac0…), so the schema is genuinely untouched. Cross-build locking measured: same process, better-sqlite3 took the write lock in 0ms while node:sqlite held it (advisory locks are per-process, single-writer silently lost); across processes it was correctly refused after 52ms with SQLITE_BUSY.

Retaken under v1's rollback journal; the previous reading was WAL-era and no longer represented this contract. 53/53 on node:sqlite, journal_mode=delete, including the two new crash vectors: SIGKILL before commit leaves nothing visible to any later reader, SIGKILL after commit never requeues. 1313 enqueues/10s, p50 7.030ms p99 12.611ms — past the 500/10s bar with 2.6x headroom under the mode actually shipped (WAL had been 3556).

53/53 on Node v22.21.0 bundling SQLite 3.50.4 — the interpreter the fleet pins and the ruling preserves. The re-derived 3.38.0 floor admits it (gate returned true); the superseded 3.51.3 WAL-era floor would have rejected it and broken fleet compatibility outright. 1299 enqueues/10s there, p99 12.958ms.

45/45 through better-sqlite3 13.0.3 (bundling 3.53.4) with only the binding swapped; migration SQL hashes identically under both (4466bac0…), so freezing node:sqlite for v1 did not make the binding part of the contract. Cross-build locking re-confirmed and unaffected by the journal-mode change: same process, the second build took the write lock in 1ms while the first held it; across processes it was refused after 52ms with SQLITE_BUSY.

9/9 flips gated under DELETE, up from 7 — added counter-examples for converting a WAL database instead of refusing it, and for putting locality detection back into protocol core. Every reported failure is one of our own assertions naming the violated claim. Guard re-verified against reality: an engine that cannot load produces only the file-level summary line, which the runner classifies as HARNESS FAILURE and exits non-zero on.

55/55 under journal_mode=delete, up from 53: adds the deterministic busy_timeout ordering gate and the integration head's handler-crash vector. 1314 enqueues/10s, p50 7.033ms p99 12.780ms. Also re-measured after making the drain consumers stop on an empty queue rather than a wall clock — they had flaked 1 in 5 on their own.
55/55 on Node v22.21.0 / SQLite 3.50.4, the interpreter the fleet pins. The new ordering gate and the drain fix both hold there too, on the older bundled engine.
45/45 through better-sqlite3 13.0.3 with only the binding swapped; unchanged by this round's work.

gated 10/10, ungated 0, not measured 0. The previous 9/9 reading was wrong in a way worth naming: busy-timeout-after-version-probe was gated only by a probabilistic race that caught it 8/12, so two honest runs disagreed. It now has a deterministic gate — canonical passes 20/20, the wrong-order stub is caught 20/20, missed 0. Runner output is three-state, and all three are exercised against one vector: GATED, UNGATED, NOT MEASURED.
